# #735 — NATS worker LaunchAgent has no installer and no liveness assertion — a deleted plist is invisible and unrecoverable by script

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-08-18T02:15:10Z
Updated: 2026-08-18T02:15:10Z

---

The durable defect behind the Aug 14-17 outage, per the #724 forensics lane (2026-08-17): the worker plist was hand-created (runbook prose only), so when something removed it (mechanism CONFIRMED: deliberate SIGTERM/bootout at 2026-08-14T14:53:35Z, per run-nats-worker.ts:243-247 being the only emitter of the observed shutdown line; deploy-strand path KILLED — local-clone-deploy.sh has no plist verbs; strongest actor candidate UNVERIFIED: CleanMyMac 5, installed 10:50 that morning, its removal-module artifacts in ~/.Trash at 11:03), nothing could detect the absence or recreate the file for three days.

Fix per the lane's finding: apply the repo's own existing pattern — scripts/install-qmd-sync-launchagent.sh (bootout+bootstrap from a checked-in docs/deploy template) — to the NATS worker label, and add a health/done-means assertion that FAILS when the worker's label is absent from launchctl. The watermark alarm (PR #728) catches the embedding symptom; this catches the service-absence cause. Refs #724.
